known_information: The original report identifies Store0.102.3001, Windows10 build19045, per-user installation and elevated execution. The visible failure is the MWB pairing banner.
The new November2reply supplies two-machine0.102.3001 observations: New key fails, handover works only one way, and hotkey switching fails from the affected side.

The new reply quotes repeated engine-side Rejected Settings IPC client: untrusted-signature and a separate sharing-violation exception while saving MWB settings. The participant reports checking one instance of each PowerToys process and reinstalling without relief.

The participant reports that offline manual configuration restored handover. This is a reported workaround, not controlled proof of the signing cause or an endorsed cross-machine key/configuration-copy procedure.
Open tracking issue50795 contains matching bidirectional Settings/MWB signature rejections and independent0.102.3001 confirmations with valid Microsoft signatures but different signer certificates.

Released NamedPipePeerVerification.MeetsSigningPolicy requires a matching trusted signer when the caller has an embedded signature; HaveMatchingSignerCertificate compares the leaf certificate bytes. This explains the tracked failure class, but no signer certificate was supplied for this particular installation.
Read complete report, all three replies, timeline and covering discussion; no existing fork design was found. New evidence replaces the prior generic request for version/action and a fresh ZIP.

fix_assessment.rationale: Existing open investigation covers the signature-rejection class. This denotes tracked work, not a released fix or proof that the file-lock exception has the same root cause.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed follow-up: it supplies the failing New key action, the two-machine version, and the engine-side `Rejected Settings IPC client: untrusted-signature` message. That rejection matches the Settings/MWB verification problem tracked in #50795, including reports on 0.102.3001. This is a local Settings-to-MWB boundary, so working input in one direction does not show that settings synchronization is healthy. Please consolidate this signature-rejection evidence under #50795; there is no need to repeat the old version/action checklist or upload the same information again. The separate settings-file sharing violation is useful evidence, but these logs do not establish which process owns the lock or that the signature rejection causes it. The offline-edit workaround is not proof of either cause; please do not publish pairing keys, copy device identities between machines, or bypass signature verification. The tracking issue is still open; this is not a claim that a fix has shipped.
